does: Sets light to a spirit poured over hot food. The flame burns away its harshness and leaves its flavour. Some of the alcohol stays in the dish.
how: Take the pan off the heat and clear the space above it.
Pour in the spirit from a ladle or a small glass, never from the bottle.
Put the pan back on the heat, lean back, and touch a long match to its edge.
Shake the pan gently until the flames die on their own.

cues.text: Blue flames that rise, then sink and go out within moments.
The sharp smell of raw spirit gives way to a warm, sweet one.

mistakes.mistake: Pouring from the bottle, so that the flame can run up the stream.
mistakes.fix: Measure the spirit into a ladle or a glass first.

mistakes.mistake: Adding the spirit to a pan that is too cool, so that it will not light and the dish tastes of raw alcohol.
mistakes.fix: Have the pan hot, and warm the spirit if need be.

mistakes.mistake: Lighting it under a low shelf or a running fan.
mistakes.fix: Clear the space above the pan before you light it.
